name: Nagatacho
tagline: Toranomon in 4 minutes and Shibuya in 9 minutes. Served by 5 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥170,000 to ¥180,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro run 5 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 10 minutes to Otemachi, 10 minutes to Shinjuku, 9 minutes to Shibuya and 18 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. The station stands 27.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.6 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 27.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 9.8 m to 29.4 m, a difference of 19.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 20 clinics and 20 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 友仁会赤坂見附前田病院, about 8 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 茂恵会半蔵門病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 5 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line also call here. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line are available too. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Namboku Line stop here as well. All 5 lines are run by Tokyo Metro, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line runs at 154%. Its busiest stretch is 新大塚→茗荷谷, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥170,000 to ¥180,000 and 1K ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. 1LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000 and 2LDK ¥490,000 to ¥500,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. 5 lines and a wide choice of connections and a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Akasaka, but Nagatacho is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nagatacho. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Nagatacho. One-room rents run about ¥12,000 lower.

neighbours.lead: Tameike-Sanno is ahead on quiet, but Nagatacho is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nagatacho. It takes 5 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Nagatacho.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速4号新宿線 viaduct runs right beside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
青山通り (4 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 5 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
